title: Cerebellopontine angle tumor with hearing loss: meningioma
vignette: A 55-year-old woman comes to the physician due to a 4-month history of progressive hearing loss in her right ear. Vital signs are within normal limits. Inspection of the external ear canals and tympanic membranes shows no abnormalities. Neurologic examination shows decreased hearing in the right ear; hearing in the left ear is normal. MRI of the head with contrast shows a homogeneously enhancing, extra-axial mass at the right cerebellopontine angle compressing the adjacent nerve. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

clues.text: progressive hearing loss in her right ear
clues.note: Unilateral, progressive sensorineural hearing loss suggests a lesion compressing the vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII).

clues.text: external ear canals and tympanic membranes shows no abnormalities
clues.note: A normal ear canal/TM points to a RETROcochlear (nerve) cause rather than a conductive/middle-ear problem.

clues.text: homogeneously enhancing, extra-axial mass at the right cerebellopontine angle
clues.note: A homogeneously enhancing EXTRA-AXIAL mass at the CEREBELLOPONTINE ANGLE compressing CN VIII is most likely a meningioma (or vestibular schwannoma).

whatMatters: A homogeneously enhancing, EXTRA-AXIAL mass at the CEREBELLOPONTINE ANGLE causing unilateral progressive sensorineural hearing loss (CN VIII compression) in a middle-aged woman is most likely a MENINGIOMA. Answer E. (Vestibular schwannoma is the other main CPA tumor; imaging/histology differentiate them.)
strategy: Localize to the cerebellopontine angle (CN VIII compression -> unilateral hearing loss) and note EXTRA-axial + homogeneous enhancement in a middle-aged woman = meningioma. Reject arteriovenous malformation (flow voids/honeycomb, seizures in young patients), astrocytoma (intra-axial/parenchymal glial tumor), ependymoma (ventricular lining/4th ventricle or spinal cord, not CPA), and medulloblastoma (children, cerebellar midline).

eliminations.label: Arteriovenous malformation - flow voids, young patients
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a congenital tangle of vessels that often causes headaches/seizures in children and young adults; on MRI it shows a honeycomb of flow voids. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is not a homogeneously enhancing extra-axial CPA mass causing progressive hearing loss. ✅ Correct if: hypointense flow voids with hemorrhage/seizures.

eliminations.label: Astrocytoma - intra-axial glial tumor
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a tumor of astrocytes arising WITHIN the brain parenchyma (intra-axial). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this mass is EXTRA-axial at the CPA; astrocytomas develop in the parenchyma, not the CPA cistern. ✅ Correct if: an intra-axial glial tumor.

eliminations.label: Ependymoma - ventricular/spinal, not CPA
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a tumor of the ependymal lining (4th ventricle in children, spinal cord in adults). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it arises in the ventricles/central canal (often with obstructive hydrocephalus), not at the cerebellopontine angle. ✅ Correct if: a 4th-ventricle or intramedullary spinal mass.

eliminations.label: Medulloblastoma - pediatric cerebellar midline
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a malignant embryonal tumor of children (age 5-9) in the cerebellar MIDLINE, causing vomiting/ataxia and hydrocephalus. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it occurs in children along the midline, not as a CPA extra-axial mass in a 55-year-old. ✅ Correct if: a midline cerebellar mass in a child.

reasoning: Unilateral progressive sensorineural hearing loss + normal ear canal/TM = retrocochlear (CN VIII) lesion
MRI shows a homogeneously enhancing EXTRA-axial mass at the cerebellopontine angle
In a middle-aged woman this is most likely a meningioma (vs vestibular schwannoma)
mechanism: Tumors at the CEREBELLOPONTINE ANGLE (CPA) - the space between the cerebellum, pons, and petrous temporal bone - compress the VESTIBULOCOCHLEAR nerve (CN VIII), causing progressive UNILATERAL sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, and imbalance; with growth they can affect the facial nerve (CN VII, facial weakness) and trigeminal nerve (CN V, facial numbness). The two most common CPA tumors are VESTIBULAR SCHWANNOMA (acoustic neuroma - often extends into the internal auditory canal) and MENINGIOMA. MENINGIOMAS are benign extra-axial tumors arising from meningothelial (arachnoid cap) cells, more common in middle-aged to elderly WOMEN; on MRI they are EXTRA-AXIAL, HOMOGENEOUSLY ENHANCING masses (often with a dural tail), and histology shows cells in whorls/lobules with PSAMMOMA BODIES. Because imaging features overlap with schwannoma, histology is often needed for definitive diagnosis; treatment is usually surgical resection. Given the homogeneously enhancing extra-axial CPA mass in this woman, meningioma is the best answer. The distractors localize elsewhere or to other populations: AVM (vascular, young), astrocytoma (intra-axial glioma), ependymoma (ventricular/spinal), and medulloblastoma (pediatric cerebellar midline).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Neuro > cerebellopontine angle tumors: vestibular schwannoma + meningioma; unilateral sensorineural hearing loss (CN VIII); meningioma = extra-axial, homogeneous enhancement, dural tail, psammoma bodies, middle-aged women.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Extra-axial, homogeneously enhancing CPA mass with hearing loss in a woman = meningioma.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on cerebellopontine angle, extra- vs intra-axial, vestibular schwannoma, psammoma bodies, or dural tail? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: AVM (flow voids), astrocytoma (intra-axial), ependymoma (ventricular/spinal), medulloblastoma (pediatric midline) don't fit a CPA extra-axial mass.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the contrast MRI: a homogeneously enhancing, extra-axial mass sits at the cerebellopontine angle (near the pons), compressing CN VIII. Anchor: 'extra-axial enhancing CPA mass + hearing loss = meningioma (vs schwannoma).'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: CPA tumors = vestibular schwannoma + meningioma; unilateral hearing loss; meningioma = whorls + psammoma bodies, women.

keywords.front: Extra-axial enhancing CPA mass + unilateral hearing loss (woman)
Two most common cerebellopontine angle tumors

keywords.back: Medulloblastoma = pediatric cerebellar midline; meningioma = adult extra-axial

firstAid.detail: Neuro: meningioma (extra-axial, homogeneous enhancement); CN VIII compression.
Neuro > arachnoid cap cells; whorls + psammoma bodies; women.

memoryHook: An extra-axial, brightly and evenly enhancing lump at the CP angle squeezing the hearing nerve in a middle-aged woman = meningioma (its cousin the schwannoma burrows into the ear canal).
